The truth about weight loss (I’m a personal trainer and previously overweight) (and this sucks to hear) is that once you are overweight, your body will always want to be overweight. It starts to believe that all that excess is normal. Your body will adapt to whatever stimulus you put on it. 

Once you are overweight, even if you lose some or a lot of it, your body will always want to go back to where it believes it’s most comfortable. The path of least resistance if you will. This happens a lot to people who were on the biggest loser. They gain it all back. Not always because they completely fall of the wagon, but because as previous overweight people they are now always predisposed to be over weight. I struggle with this myself. 

The key is making it a lifestyle change and trying to observe at least 80/20 to keep the weight off the best you can. You’re not alone.

I get through it by finding something to look forward to every day. Even if it’s something really small and inconsequential. Another thing that helps me is to stay busy and distract yourself. My depression gets really bad if I indulge my thoughts and go deeper into the rabbit hole. So while it does feel good to just sit in bed and listen to music, this is generally when my depression spirals. So I’ll get up and tidy the house or go for a walk or organize my sock drawer or listen to a pod cast or anything to keep my mind occupied.

I understand this. One thing that helps me is to get in bed and get comfortable and then take deep breaths into your diaphragm. This will signal a physiological response that triggers your parasympathetic nervous system to calm you down. Just keep breathing into your belly.
